title: Coinduction transitivity on a double finite projective resolution
statement:
Let $S\to B\to D$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with coinduction $C_B^S,C_D^B,C_D^S$ and their precomposition actions [def-trf-derived-coinduction], product total Hom [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], and signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Here a finitely generated projective module means a direct summand of a finite free module. Let $a:P\to B[0]$ be an augmented bounded complex of finitely generated projective $S$-modules, a quasi-isomorphism, and let $Q$ be another bounded complex of finitely generated projective $S$-modules. Suppose an augmentation $b:B\otimes_S Q\to D[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism of $B$-complexes. Set $W=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_S Q)$, with augmentation $w=b(a\otimes1)$. Then $w$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For every $S$-complex $N$, choose a K-injective resolution $j:N\to I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and put $J=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(B[0],I)$. There is a commuting diagram of quasi-isomorphisms of $S$-complexes
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
U\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(D[0],J)&\xrightarrow{\ e\ }&\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(D[0],I)\\
\downarrow b^*&&\downarrow w^*\\
U\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(B\otimes_S Q,J)&\xrightarrow{\ \kappa\ }&\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(W,I),
\end{array}$$
where $U$ is restriction to $S$, $e(h)(d)=h(d)(1)$, and $\kappa$ is the composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(B\otimes_S Q,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(Q,J)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Hom}(Q,a^*)}\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(Q,\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P,I))
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_S P),I)
\xrightarrow{(\sigma_{P,Q})^*}\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(W,I).$$
The first map evaluates at $1\otimes q$; $a^*$ is precomposition with $a$; currying evaluates $h(q)(p)$ without a sign; and $\sigma_{P,Q}(p\otimes q)=(-1)^{ij}q\otimes p$ for $p\in P^i$, $q\in Q^j$. The top horizontal map localizes to the scalar restriction of the canonical right-adjoint composition comparison $C_D^B C_B^S([N])\xrightarrow{\sim}C_D^S([N])$, whose counit is the composite of the evaluation-at-one counits. Thus the bottom comparison, using the displayed quasi-isomorphisms as model identifications, computes that actual comparison, including its derived $D$-action. The map $\operatorname{Hom}_S(W,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(W,I)$ induced by $j$ is also a quasi-isomorphism. These identifications are natural in $N$ and in maps of the two augmented resolutions and are independent of $j$ through the canonical derived comparisons. No flatness of $B/S$ or $D/B$, Noetherianity, or boundedness of $N$ is imposed.

proof.text: First, $W$ is bounded with finite projective terms. If $P^i$ and $Q^j$ are retracts of $S^{r_i}$ and $S^{s_j}$, tensoring their inclusion/retraction maps exhibits $P^i\otimes_SQ^j$ as a retract of $S^{r_is_j}$. Each $W^n$ is a finite direct sum of such retracts, since $P,Q$ are bounded. The direct sums of the inclusion/retraction maps exhibit $W^n$ as a retract of a finite free module.

source.place: Finite retract calculation for the explicit total tensor; agent argument

proof.text: Each term of $Q$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $Q$ K-flat. Apply the quasi-isomorphism criterion of [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] to $a:P\to B[0]$. It gives the quasi-isomorphism $a\otimes1:W\to B\otimes_SQ$. Restriction from $B$ to $S$ does not change the groups or kernels and images of the differentials, so $b$ is also a quasi-isomorphism over $S$. On each cohomology group $H^n(w)=H^n(b)H^n(a\otimes1)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 064K, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism; Tag 06XZ, definition-K-flat and lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism

proof.text: For later use, a quasi-isomorphism $t:X\to Y$ induces a quasi-isomorphism $t^*:\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(Y,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(X,I)$ whenever $I$ is K-injective. Indeed [lem-sc-module-hom-complex-quotient] and [lem-sc-hom-cocycle-homotopy-quotient-formulas] identify degree-$n$ Hom cohomology with maps $X\to I[n]$ modulo homotopy: cycles are chain maps to the shifted target and boundaries are null homotopies. Apply [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison] to $I[n]$, which is K-injective by translating the null-homotopy definition. Under these identifications $H^n(t^*)$ is precomposition with the invertible localized map $[t]$, hence is bijective for every $n$. The identifications commute with precomposition because they send a cycle to its own homotopy class.

By [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model] for $S\to B$, $J=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(B[0],I)$ is K-injective over $B$. The same node, now applied to the $B$-complex $D[0]$, gives exactly $e$, with inverse $g\mapsto(d\mapsto(c\mapsto g(cd)))$ for $c\in B$. Thus $e$ is a chain isomorphism. Apply step 3 over $B$ to $b$ and $J$, and over $S$ to $w$ and $I$. This proves that $b^*$ and $w^*$ are quasi-isomorphisms, with no claim that $UJ$ is K-injective over $S$.

The first arrow defining $\kappa$ is the chain isomorphism $F\mapsto(q\mapsto F(1\otimes q))$ with inverse $h\mapsto(c\otimes q\mapsto c\,h(q))$. Balancing and the inverse identities are $B$-linearity; both formulas commute with the differential since $B[0]$ is in degree zero. Precomposition $a^*:J\to\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P,I)$ is a chain map, so applying product Hom from $Q$ gives a chain map by the displayed Hom differential. For the next arrow specialize [lem-trf-bimodule-chain-currying-descent] to the identity ring map $S\to S$, with $A=Q$, $T=P$, $N=I$. It is the entire-complex isomorphism $h\mapsto(q\otimes p\mapsto h(q)(p))$, without an extra sign.

source.place: Tag 0A5Y, lemma-compose; mixed-ring version in dga.tex Tag 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction

proof.text: The flip $\sigma:P\otimes Q\to Q\otimes P$ is a chain isomorphism. For $p\in P^i,q\in Q^j$, $d\sigma(p\otimes q)$ has terms $(-1)^{ij}dq\otimes p$ and $(-1)^{ij+j}q\otimes dp$. The terms of $\sigma d(p\otimes q)$ have exponents $i+i(j+1)\equiv ij$ and $(i+1)j=ij+j$, respectively. Flipping twice gives the identity since $2ij$ is even. Consequently precomposition by $\sigma$ is a chain isomorphism of the product Hom complexes. Combining this with step 5 constructs the specified chain map $\kappa$.

source.place: Sign rules preceding lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes; explicit signed flip verification

proof.text:
Check the square on a homogeneous cochain $h:D[0]\to J$ and a pure tensor $p\otimes q$ of degrees $(i,j)$. Its bottom-left path has value $(-1)^{ij}h(b(1\otimes q))(a(p))$; its top-right path has value $h(b(a(p)\otimes q))(1)$. If $i\ne0$ then $a(p)=0$ and both vanish. For $i=0$ the sign is $1$, and $B$-linearity of $h$ and $b$ gives
$$h(b(1\otimes q))(a(p))=(a(p)h(b(1\otimes q)))(1)=h(b(a(p)\otimes q))(1).$$
The formulas extend additively to each total degree, proving strict commutativity. On cohomology $H^n(\kappa)H^n(b^*)=H^n(w^*)H^n(e)$; the other three factors are isomorphisms by step 4, so $H^n(\kappa)$ is an isomorphism. This proves all four displayed arrows are quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0C0F, lemma-composition-right-adjoints: explicit augmentation-normalized representative square (agent calculation)

proof.text: The two top complexes are the coinduction models for $C_D^BC_B^S([N])$ and $C_D^S([N])$: $J$ is K-injective over $B$ by step 4 and $I$ is K-injective over $S$. The actions on both are precomposition in $d\in D$. Thus $e(th)(d)=h(dt)(1)=(t\,e(h))(d)$, so $e$ is $D$-linear before localization. By [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] each coinduction is right adjoint to restriction with evaluation-at-one counit, independent of resolutions. For the composite adjunction the counit at $h$ is $h(1_D)(1_B)$, obtained by the two successive evaluations. Evaluation of $e(h)$ at $1_D$ has exactly this value. Hence the localized $D$-linear map $e$ is counit-compatible. By [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] it is the canonical right-adjoint composition comparison, with its specified orientation.

Let $L=[U\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_SQ,J)]$ and $R=[\operatorname{Hom}_S(W,I)]$ in $D(S)$. Use $[b^*]^{-1}$ to identify $L$ with the scalar restriction of $C_D^BC_B^S([N])$, and $[w^*]^{-1}$ to identify $R$ with that of $C_D^S([N])$. The square says
$$[w^*]^{-1}[\kappa][b^*]=[e].$$
Give $L,R$ the derived $D$-module structures transported through these very model identifications from the two top $D$-objects. Step 8 and this equality identify the bottom arrow with the actual comparison, including that action. No strict $D$-action on $P,Q,W$ is assumed or needed.

source.place: Tag 0C0F, lemma-composition-right-adjoints: interpretation of the explicit representative square

proof.text: By step 1, $W$ is bounded above with projective terms, so [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] makes it K-projective. Combine [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] with the Hom cohomology/homotopy identifications of step 3, now with fixed source $W$. For every $n$, the homology map induced by $\operatorname{Hom}_S(W,j)$ identifies with postcomposition by $[j[n]]$ on $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}([W],[N[n]])$. This is a bijection since $j$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Therefore $\operatorname{Hom}_S(W,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(W,I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism even for unbounded $N$.

source.place: Dual K-projective form of Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; more-algebra.tex Tag 0A8H, equation-cohomology-hom-complex

proof.text: For augmentation-preserving maps $u:P'\to P$, $v:Q'\to Q$ one has $a u=a'$ and $b(1\otimes v)=b'$. The value of the precomposed bottom formula at $p'\otimes q'$ is $(-1)^{ij}F(1\otimes v(q'))(a(u(p')))$, which equals the formula using the new augmentations. A chain map $I\to I'$ commutes with these formulas by postcomposition. Currying has precisely this naturality by [lem-trf-bimodule-chain-currying-descent], while $e$ has it by [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model]. For a derived coefficient morphism, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents it by a unique homotopy class of maps between chosen K-injectives, so the chain-map equalities descend. In particular the comparison between $j:N\to I$ and $j':N\to I'$ is the homotopy class representing $[j'][j]^{-1}$; the same bijection says its composite with $j$ is homotopic to $j'$. The resolution independence in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] then identifies the top maps canonically. The invertible vertical identifications force exactly the same independence and naturality for the bottom map. None of these arguments uses flatness of either ring map, Noetherianity, or a bound on $N$.
